You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From dfbc282c2e16cd6044e4181f150dbd1e2224eaa7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2014 11:49:17 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] check multiple parser methods are not defined in a parser

This fixes a bug introduced in be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf.

The old commit(be4a21) checked only the case that allparser, parser2 and parser_with_gc
were not set but didn't check more than one were set. This patch checks this case, too.

Signed-off-by: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>

diff --git a/parse.c b/parse.c
index 557228d1d..2ae586ea0 100644
--- a/parse.c
+++ b/parse.c
@@ -969,7 +969,7 @@ extern void initializeParsing (void)
 				accepted = TRUE;
 #endif
 			}
-			else if ((def->parser == NULL)  &&  (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
+			else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
 				error (FATAL,
 		"%s parser definition must define one and only one parsing routine\n",
 					   def->name);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications:

**File Modified: `parse.c`**
- A conditional check in the `initializeParsing` function was updated. 
- The original check confirmed that all parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, `parser_with_gc`) were not set to NULL. 
- The new check ensures that exactly one of the parser methods is defined, changing the condition to:
  ```c
  else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
  ```
  
### Relationships:
- This modification addresses a bug from a previous commit (`be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf`) which only checked if all parser methods were unset. The new logic is more robust as it prevents the scenario where multiple parser methods are defined simultaneously, thereby ensuring that the parser definition follows the intended constraint of having exactly one valid parsing routine defined.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
else if (def->parser == NULL && def->parser2 == NULL && def->parser_with_gc == NULL)
```
Reason:
This statement only checks if all parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, and `parser_with_gc`) are unset (NULL), which allows for the possibility of multiple parser methods being defined simultaneously without raising an error. This violates the requirement that only one parser method should be defined.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
```
Reason:
This updated condition checks that exactly one of the parser methods is defined by summing the truth values of each parser method. If the sum is not equal to one, it raises an error, ensuring that only one parser method can be defined at a time, thus fixing the bug.
